panel.clean: No issues found. This BOM is ready for export.

editor.exportBlocked: Export blocked: fix the validation errors first.

rules.title: Validation Rules
rules.subtitle: Rules run on demand against a BOM. Errors block CSV export; warnings do not.

checkLabels.UniqueChildBsObjectId: No duplicate BS Object ID under one parent

checks.RequiredField: The target field must not be empty.
checks.NumericField: The target field must be a number when it is filled in. Parameters lists literal values to allow anyway, e.g. Formula.
checks.AllowedValues: The target field must match one of the values in Parameters. Empty values are ignored.
checks.MaxLength: The target field must not be longer than the number of characters in Parameters.
checks.ReleaseTemplateExists: A release template that is filled in must match an active template. Empty values are ignored — use Required field to demand one.
checks.RouteCodeExists: A route that is filled in must match an active route. Empty values are ignored — use Required field to demand one.
checks.UniqueChildBsObjectId: Two lines under the same parent must not share a BS Object ID.
checks.MaxDepth: No line may sit deeper than the level given in Parameters.
checks.PlmExpressionRequired: When the source field chosen in Target field (conditions or formula) is filled in, its translated PLM column must be filled in too.
checks.PhantomMustHaveChildren: A phantom line must have at least one child line.

form.name: Name
form.targetFieldHint: Leave empty for checks that span the whole BOM.

targetFieldFor.RequiredField: The BOM column that must not be empty.
targetFieldFor.NumericField: The BOM column that must hold a number.
targetFieldFor.AllowedValues: The BOM column whose value is checked against the list below.
targetFieldFor.MaxLength: The BOM column whose length is checked.
targetFieldFor.PlmExpressionRequired: Choose conditions or formula — it decides which pair of columns is compared.

form.parametersHint: A number, or a comma-separated list, depending on the check.

parametersFor.NumericField: Text values to accept even though they are not numbers — the source CSV writes Formula into numeric columns. Separate several with commas, or leave empty to demand a strict number.
parametersFor.AllowedValues: The values that are allowed, separated by commas.
parametersFor.MaxLength: The largest number of characters allowed.

form.appliesToStatusesHint: Leave empty to run the rule whatever state the BOM is in. Pick one or more statuses to run it only then — the BOM's status at the moment Validate or Export runs is what counts.
form.appliesWhenIntro: Limit the rule to part of the BOM. With no conditions it checks every line.
form.appliesWhenHint: Operators: = != > >= < <= contains startswith in (a,b) not in (a,b) is empty / is not empty. Combine with and / or.
form.notBuildable: This condition is too complex for the builder, so it stays as text.

delete.confirmMessage: Delete rule "{{name}}"? This cannot be undone.

builder.empty: No conditions — the rule checks every line.

help.title: How to define a validation rule
help.intro: A rule is a single check the app runs over a BOM when someone presses Validate. You choose what is checked, which lines it applies to, and how serious a failure is.

flow.title: How a rule works
flow.step1: The BOM is loaded. Deleted lines are skipped entirely.
flow.step2: If the rule has an “Applies when” condition, only the lines matching it are kept.
flow.step3: The chosen check runs on those lines, using Target field and Parameters as its arguments.
flow.step4: Each failure appears in the Validation results panel at the chosen severity. Errors block CSV export; warnings do not.

code.title: Code
code.body: A short, stable identifier shown next to every issue the rule reports, for example REQ-ROUTE. Use capitals and hyphens.
code.note: It must be unique and cannot be changed after the rule is created, because it is how people refer to the rule.

name.title: Name
name.body: A plain description of the rule for this admin list, for example “Route is required on assemblies”. It is not shown to the people validating BOMs — that is what Message is for.

check.title: Check
check.body: The logic that runs. This is the most important choice: each check answers a different question, and picking the wrong one is the usual reason a rule reports nothing.

severity.title: Severity
severity.error: blocks CSV export and blocks submitting the BOM for review until it is fixed.
severity.warning: is listed in the results panel but never blocks anything.
severity.note: Start new rules as warnings. Promote them to errors once the existing BOMs are clean, otherwise every export is blocked on day one.

targetField.title: Target field
targetField.body: The BOM column the check looks at. Required for Required field, Numeric field, Allowed values and Maximum length.
targetField.plm: For “PLM expression is filled in”, choose conditions or formula — it decides which pair of columns is compared.
targetField.note: Checks marked “Not used” in the table above ignore this box completely, so leave it empty for them.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.body: An extra argument whose meaning depends on the check. The Check table above lists exactly what each one expects. A check that does not use it leaves the box greyed out.
parameters.number: Maximum length and Maximum depth: a single number, for example 60 or 8.
parameters.list: Allowed values: a comma-separated list, for example PART, PURCHASED, ASSEMBLY.
parameters.literals: Numeric field: text values to accept even though they are not numbers, separated by commas.
parameters.formulaNote: This is why the supplied “Final quantity must be numeric” rule has Formula in its Parameters box: the exported CSV writes the word Formula into numeric columns where the value is calculated in PLM. Remove it and every one of those lines is reported as an error.

appliesWhen.title: Applies when
appliesWhen.body: An optional filter that narrows the rule to part of the BOM. Leave it empty and the rule checks every line. This is how you express exceptions such as “only lines that are not phantom”.
appliesWhen.shape: Each condition is written as: field, operator, value.
appliesWhen.combiningBody: Join conditions with and / or. There are no brackets: every or splits the expression first, so “a and b or c” means “(a and b) or c”. Spaces around and / or are required; spaces around the operator are optional.
appliesWhen.specialFields: Fields that are not BOM columns
appliesWhen.level: level — the depth in the tree, where a top-level line is 1.
appliesWhen.hasChildren: hasChildren — true when the line has at least one child line, so it is an assembly rather than a single part. Deleted children do not count.
appliesWhen.booleans: phantom, isEbom and hasChildren are true or false. Compare them with = true or = false.
appliesWhen.note: A condition that cannot be understood is rejected when you save, so a typo can never silently switch a rule off.

appliesToStatuses.title: Applies to BOM status
appliesToStatuses.body: An optional list of BOM statuses the rule runs in. Use it when a requirement only has to be met later in the lifecycle — for example a BS Object ID that is only assigned once the BOM has been approved.
appliesToStatuses.empty: Leave the box empty and the rule runs whatever state the BOM is in. That is how every supplied rule is set up.
appliesToStatuses.evaluation: The rule is judged against the status the BOM is in at the moment the check runs, never the status it is moving to. That matters at each gate:
appliesToStatuses.gateSubmit: Submitting a Draft for review runs the rules that apply to Draft.
appliesToStatuses.gateApprove: Approving a BOM that is In review runs the rules that apply to In review.
appliesToStatuses.gateRelease: Releasing an Approved BOM runs the rules that apply to Approved — this is where an “Approved only” rule bites.
appliesToStatuses.gateExport: Exporting the CSV runs the rules that apply to the BOM's current status.
appliesToStatuses.note: A forward step is blocked while any error remains. Moving a BOM back to Draft is never blocked, so a BOM can always be sent back to be fixed.

message.title: Message shown to the user
message.body: The sentence shown in the Validation results panel. Write it as an instruction to the person fixing the BOM. You can insert:
message.value: {value} — the offending value on the line.
message.note: If you leave this empty a generic English sentence is used instead.

active.title: Active
active.body: Switch a rule off to stop it running without deleting it, and without losing its history. Inactive rules are skipped completely.

contains.meaning: the text appears anywhere in the value

startswith.meaning: the value begins with the text

in.meaning: matches one of the listed values

notIn.meaning: matches none of the listed values

assemblies.goal: Only assemblies that are really manufactured

staged.goal: Skip lines staged for deletion in PLM

withCondition.goal: Only lines that already carry a rule in plain language

walkthrough.title: Worked example
walkthrough.goal: “Every manufactured assembly must have a route, but phantoms and single parts do not.”
walkthrough.message: Route is required on manufactured assemblies.
walkthrough.note: Note the check: Required field, not Route is defined. “Route is defined” only verifies a route that is already filled in, so on its own it would never notice a missing one.
